newsitem.title: UK: British meat inspectors warn of abattoir time bomb.
newsitem.headline: British meat inspectors warn of abattoir time bomb.

text.p: The body which represents inspectors of meat processed by British abattoirs has warned of "a potential time bomb" because of falling standards of hygiene, documents made available to journalists on Tuesday showed.

The Meat Inspectors Association warned the government last month faecal contamination of carcases, blamed for an outbreak of food poisoning in Scotland which killed 20 people, "appears to be becoming an acceptable infringement of regulations".
The warning came in a letter to junior agriculture minister Angela Browning from the Association's general secretary Peter Comrie.

The opposition Labour Party, which last week accused the government of covering up a report on abattoir standards, published Comrie's letter along with two others to Johnston McNeil, chief executive of the Meat Hygiene Service.
In January, Comrie told McNeil: "It appears from the very many phone calls from members that far from improving, standards of hygiene are steadily decreasing."
"There is no need to tell you that this is a potential timebomb, and I would urge you to implement measures, as in the BSE (mad cow disease) crisis, in order to overcome this dangerous situation."
